title: NCLEX-RN Examinations (CAT & Next-Gen NGN Mock Suite)
subtitle: Dedicated NCLEX-RN simulation course featuring timed 60–100 question examinations across all 8 NCSBN Client Needs categories with verified Saunders & Kaplan rationales.

exams.title: Exam 1: NCLEX-RN Diagnostic Readiness Examination (75 Questions)
exams.description: Balanced diagnostic simulation across Safe & Effective Care, Health Promotion, Psychosocial & Physiological Integrity.

questions.prompt: Question: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a rash on the scalp characterized by greasy, yellow scales. The nurse should document this finding as which of the following?
options: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap)
Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
Tinea capitis (ringworm)
Impetigo
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching the parents of a 1-year-old child with eczema about skin care. Which of the following should be included in the teaching?
options: Bathe the child daily with hot water and soap
Apply a moisturizer to the child's skin while it's still damp
Dress the child in wool or synthetic fabrics
Use perfumed lotions to soothe the skin
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Apply a moisturizer to the child's skin while it's still damp (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer alpha blockers
Check catecholamine levels
Encourage relaxation techniques
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Alpha blockers help control blood pressure and reduce symptoms.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 12: Sensory System (Eye & Ear Disorders) & Perioperative Care, what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
questions.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma is prescribed a short-acting beta2-agonist and a glucocorticoid inhaler. Which medication should the nurse instruct the patient to use first?
options: The beta2-agonist
The glucocorticoid
Either can be used first
Neither, they should be used simultaneously
questions.rationale: The short-acting beta2-agonist should be used first to dilate the bronchioles and improve airflow. This will then enhance the distribution and absorption of the glucocorticoid inhaler.

questions.prompt: A patient presents with a sudden onset of dyspnea. The nurse auscultates the lung and hears a high-pitched sound on inspiration. What could this indicate?
options: Stridor
Crackles
Wheezing
Pleural friction rub
questions.rationale: Stridor is a high-pitched, inspiratory sound that is often heard in acute laryngeal obstruction. It is a medical emergency and requires immediate attention.

questions.prompt: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic for a well-baby check-up. Which of the following developmental milestones would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Sitting without support
Rolling over from back to stomach
Smiling in response to familiar faces
Walking with support
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Smiling in response to familiar faces (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A client managed for Respiratory A&P, Breath Sounds, ABGs, Thoracentesis & Chest Tubes develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Respiratory A&P, Breath Sounds, ABGs, Thoracentesis & Chest Tubes, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer metoclopramide
Check blood glucose levels
Encourage fluid intake
Provide nutritional support
questions.rationale: Metoclopramide enhances gastric motility.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing dyspnea and is diagnosed with pulmonary edema. Which of the following actions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Position the patient in a high Fowler’s position.
Encourage deep breathing and coughing.
Auscultate lung sounds bilaterally.
Administer prescribed diuretics.
questions.rationale: The high Fowler's position reduces venous return to the heart, thereby decreasing pulmonary congestion and improving the patient's breathing.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Take Action under NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM). Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Ignore abnormal trends in Take Action unless the client requests medication.
Delay intervention and document Take Action at end of shift.
Delegate initial assessment of Take Action to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Assess the patient first unless immediate life-saving action is clear (e.g., apply oxygen for SpO2 84%, stop IV infusion for anaphylaxis, raise HOB for dyspnea).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM), Take Action requires: Assess the patient first unless immediate life-saving action is clear (e.g., apply oxygen for SpO2 84%, stop IV infusion for anaphylaxis, raise HOB for dyspnea).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing thyroid storm. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer beta blockers
Check thyroid hormone levels
Encourage rest
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Beta blockers control symptoms like tachycardia.

questions.prompt: A patient has just undergone enucleation of the eye due to ocular melanoma. What is the nurse's priority in the immediate postoperative care of this patient?
options: Ensuring the patient's pain is controlled
Educating the patient about the use of an ocular prosthesis
Monitoring the surgical site for bleeding
Providing emotional support to the patient
questions.rationale: While all of these actions are important, the nurse's immediate postoperative priority is to monitor the surgical site for bleeding or other complications. Pain control, patient education about an ocular prosthesis, and emotional support will follow once the patient is medically stable.

questions.prompt: The nurse is preparing to administer a vaccine to a 2-month-old infant. Which site is the most appropriate for this injection?
options: The deltoid muscle
The ventrogluteal site
The vastus lateralis muscle
The dorsogluteal site
questions.rationale: Correct answer: The vastus lateralis muscle (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with HIV/AIDS (CD4 < 200) (HIV/AIDS Staging, CD4 Counts, Opportunistic Infections & ART). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Risk for Pneumocystis (PCP), TB, Kaposi sarcoma, candidiasis.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For HIV/AIDS (CD4 < 200), the priority intervention is: Risk for Pneumocystis (PCP), TB, Kaposi sarcoma, candidiasis. Key exam watchpoint: Strict ART adherence (>95% doses); TMP-SMX (Bactrim) prophylaxis when CD4 < 200.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who has undergone chemotherapy. Which of the following instructions should be included?
options: "Your child should avoid crowds and people with infections."
"Your child can return to school and engage in physical activities."
"Your child should eat a diet high in raw fruits and vegetables."
"Your child can receive live virus vaccines."
questions.rationale: Children who have undergone chemotherapy have a suppressed immune system and are more susceptible to infections. They should avoid crowds and people with infections to minimize the risk of getting sick.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child presents with itchy, red, scaly patches on the elbows and knees. The nurse recognizes this as a chronic skin condition often seen in children with a family history of allergies. What is the likely diagnosis?
options: Psoriasis
Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
Contact dermatitis
Impetigo
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer albuterol to a patient with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse monitor for as a potential side effect of this medication?
options: Bradycardia
Hypotension
Tachycardia
Hypoglycaemia
questions.rationale: Albuterol, a beta2-adrenergic agonist, can cause tachycardia as a side effect. It stimulates the beta2 receptors in the lungs causing bronchodilation, but it can also stimulate beta1 receptors in the heart causing increased heart rate.

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
options: Loss of peripheral vision
Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who suddenly becomes restless and anxious, with increased heart rate and decreased oxygen saturation. The nurse assesses decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Notify the physician immediately
Increase the rate of IV fluids
Position the patient on the left side
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest a pneumothorax, a medical emergency. The nurse should notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.prompt: A patient who underwent a myringotomy report experiencing pain in the ear. What should the nurse's initial response be?
options: Administer prescribed pain medication
Report the pain to the healthcare provider
Reassure the patient that pain is normal after this procedure
Check the patient's ear for signs of infection
questions.rationale: While some discomfort might be expected after a myringotomy, severe or increasing pain could indicate a complication such as infection. Therefore, the nurse should first check the patient's ear for signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, and discharge. Option A could be appropriate after the nurse has assessed the patient and ruled out complications. Option B might be appropriate if signs of infection are found. Option C is incorrect because it could delay treatment of a potential complication.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been prescribed ipratropium bromide. What is the primary action of this medication?
options: Decreases inflammation in the airways
Causes bronchodilation
Thins respiratory secretions
Suppresses the cough reflex
questions.rationale: Ipratropium bromide is an anticholinergic bronchodilator. It works by blocking the action of acetylcholine in bronchial smooth muscle, resulting in bronchodilation.

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Assess vs. Implement Rule under High-Yield NCLEX Test-Taking Strategies (ABCs, Maslow & Safety). Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Delay intervention and document Assess vs. Implement Rule at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in Assess vs. Implement Rule unless the client requests medication.
Delegate initial assessment of Assess vs. Implement Rule to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).

If the stem gives an incomplete assessment (e.g., client complains of calf pain), assess first (inspect/measure/vital signs) rather than intervening blindly — Exception: obvious life threat like choking, ventricular fibrillation, or blood transfusion reaction (stop infusion immediately).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for High-Yield NCLEX Test-Taking Strategies (ABCs, Maslow & Safety), Assess vs. Implement Rule requires: If the stem gives an incomplete assessment (e.g., client complains of calf pain), assess first (inspect/measure/vital signs) rather than intervening blindly — Exception: obvious life threat like choking, ventricular fibrillation, or blood transfusion reaction (stop infusion immediately).

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted to the emergency department with severe difficulty breathing, cyanosis, and a respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute. The nurse notes absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Prepare the patient for chest tube insertion
Administer supplemental oxygen
Initiate cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
questions.rationale: The patient's symptoms suggest a tension pneumothorax, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate decompression with chest tube insertion.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Chest Tube (Water-Seal) (COPD, Asthma, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism & ARDS). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Continuous gentle bubbling in suction chamber = normal; tidaling in water seal = normal.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
questions.rationale: For Chest Tube (Water-Seal), the priority intervention is: Continuous gentle bubbling in suction chamber = normal; tidaling in water seal = normal. Key exam watchpoint: Intermittent bubbling is OK; continuous bubbling in water seal = air leak. If dislodged, tape 3 sides!

questions.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
options: Visual system
Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
questions.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Metabolic Alkalosis (Mastering Arterial Blood Gases (ABGs) & Acid-Base Compensation). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
pH > 7.45, HCO3 > 26, PaCO2 normal/high
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
questions.rationale: For Metabolic Alkalosis, the priority intervention is: pH > 7.45, HCO3 > 26, PaCO2 normal/high Key exam watchpoint: NG suctioning, vomiting, excess antacids/diuretics. Replace fluids & KCl, treat vomiting.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old child weighing 15 kg is prescribed a medication at a dose of 50 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 75 mg
100 mg
200 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 187.5 mg (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Major Burns & Airway (Fractures, Traction Safety, Fat Embolism & Compartment Syndrome (6 Ps)). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Singed nasal hairs, soot in sputum, hoarseness = inhalation injury!
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Major Burns & Airway, the priority intervention is: Singed nasal hairs, soot in sputum, hoarseness = inhalation injury! Key exam watchpoint: Intubate/O2 early. Parkland: 4 mL x kg x %TBSA (LR) -> give 1/2 in first 8 hrs from time of burn.

questions.prompt: The nurse is providing discharge teaching for the parents of an infant with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Which instruction should be included?
options: Feed the infant larger, less frequent meals
Position the infant flat after feeding
Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal
Change the formula to a cow's milk-based formula
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000) (Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency!
questions.rationale: For Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000), the priority intervention is: Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency! Key exam watchpoint: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse include in the child's asthma action plan?
options: Teach the child to recognize and avoid triggers
Instruct the child to use a short-acting bronchodilator daily
Encourage the child to participate in sports without restrictions
Advise the child to decrease fluid intake to reduce mucus production
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Teach the child to recognize and avoid triggers (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
3 mL
5 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 2 mL (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Abruptio Placentae under Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Painful dark red bleeding, rigid board-like abdomen, fetal distress — emergency delivery priority.
Delegate initial assessment of Abruptio Placentae to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Ignore abnormal trends in Abruptio Placentae unless the client requests medication.
Delay intervention and document Abruptio Placentae at end of shift.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, Abruptio Placentae requires: Painful dark red bleeding, rigid board-like abdomen, fetal distress — emergency delivery priority.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Pyloric Stenosis vs. Intussusception (Pyloric Stenosis, Intussusception, Rheumatic Fever & Pediatric mg/kg). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Pyloric: Olive-shaped RUQ mass, projectile non-bilious vomiting. Intussusception: Currant-jelly stools, sausage mass.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Pyloric Stenosis vs. Intussusception, the priority intervention is: Pyloric: Olive-shaped RUQ mass, projectile non-bilious vomiting. Intussusception: Currant-jelly stools, sausage mass. Key exam watchpoint: Correct dehydration/electrolytes before pyloromyotomy; air/hydrostatic enema for intussusception.

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a measuring cup.
Use a syringe without a needle.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Use a syringe without a needle. (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Least Invasive to Most Invasive under High-Yield NCLEX Test-Taking Strategies (ABCs, Maslow & Safety). Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Ignore abnormal trends in Least Invasive to Most Invasive unless the client requests medication.
Try repositioning, deep breathing/coughing, and oxygen before suctioning or intubation; try bladder scan/running water before straight catheterization.
Delegate initial assessment of Least Invasive to Most Invasive to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Delay intervention and document Least Invasive to Most Invasive at end of shift.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for High-Yield NCLEX Test-Taking Strategies (ABCs, Maslow & Safety), Least Invasive to Most Invasive requires: Try repositioning, deep breathing/coughing, and oxygen before suctioning or intubation; try bladder scan/running water before straight catheterization.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The patient reports increased shortness of breath and a productive cough. What should be the nurse's primary action?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Increase the patient's oxygen flow rate
Perform a respiratory assessment
Initiate a breathing treatment
questions.rationale: Before initiating treatment, the nurse should first perform a thorough respiratory assessment to gather data about the patient's current condition. This will help guide further interventions and treatments.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Cardiac Medications: ACEi, Beta-Blockers, Digoxin, Heparin & Warfarin develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Cardiac Medications: ACEi, Beta-Blockers, Digoxin, Heparin & Warfarin, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for several patients on a busy medical-surgical unit. Which of the following patients should the nurse prioritize?
options: A patient with a history of macular degeneration who needs assistance with meal setup
A patient with a hearing aid who needs the batteries changed
A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes
A patient with a new prescription for eyeglasses who needs education about care
questions.rationale: Correct answer: A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing RED (Immediate — Emergent)?
options: Airway obstruction, tension pneumothorax, active arterial hemorrhage, shock.
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of RED (Immediate — Emergent).
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
1st Priority — Life-threatening but salvageable within 1 hr.
questions.rationale: When caring for RED (Immediate — Emergent), avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Airway obstruction, tension pneumothorax, active arterial hemorrhage, shock.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Alcohol Withdrawal (DTs) (Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Tremors, hallucinations, autonomic hyperactivity (48–72 hrs post-stop).
questions.rationale: For Alcohol Withdrawal (DTs), the priority intervention is: Tremors, hallucinations, autonomic hyperactivity (48–72 hrs post-stop). Key exam watchpoint: Administer Benzodiazepines (Lorazepam / Chlordiazepoxide), CIWA scoring, thiamine (B1).

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
questions.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who reports a sudden loss of hearing in one ear. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Administer prescribed ear drops
Schedule the patient for a hearing test
Report the symptom to the healthcare provider
Clean the patient's ear canal
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Report the symptom to the healthcare provider (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient has been diagnosed with cataracts. Which of the following statements made by the patient indicates a need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to avoid bright lights."
"I will need surgery to remove the cataracts."
"I will be able to see better after the cataracts are removed."
"Cataracts can be prevented by wearing sunglasses."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "Cataracts can be prevented by wearing sunglasses." (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Fractures, Traction Safety, Fat Embolism & Compartment Syndrome (6 Ps). Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Fractures, Traction Safety, Fat Embolism & Compartment Syndrome (6 Ps) requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Thyroid Storm vs. Myxedema (Diabetes Mellitus, DKA vs. HHS & Insulin Peak/Onset Profiles). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Storm: Fever > 104°F, HR > 140, delirium. Myxedema: Hypothermia, bradycardia, coma.
questions.rationale: For Thyroid Storm vs. Myxedema, the priority intervention is: Storm: Fever > 104°F, HR > 140, delirium. Myxedema: Hypothermia, bradycardia, coma. Key exam watchpoint: Storm: PTU, iodine, beta-blockers, cooling (NO aspirin!). Myxedema: IV Levothyroxine + warming.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing weight gain and hypertension. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease cortisol production
Increase cortisol production
Regulate blood pressure
Reduce weight
questions.rationale: Reducing cortisol levels manages symptoms.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient reports vertigo and tinnitus. This patient is most likely experiencing which of the following conditions?
options: Glaucoma
Meniere's disease
Cataracts

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Retinal Detachment (Glaucoma, Cataracts, Retinal Detachment & Eye Drop Administration). What is the priority nursing action?

Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?

Central vision loss

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Appendicitis & Peritonitis (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?

Impetigo
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient is lethargic and unresponsive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Administer oxygen
Position the patient on their side
Prepare for intubation
Initiate CPR
questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute is dangerously low and indicates respiratory failure. The patient is unresponsive, suggesting a lack of oxygen to the brain. Immediate intervention, such as intubation, is needed.

questions.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?

Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
questions.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child weighing 15 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 20 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 50 mg
100 mg
200 mg
300 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 100 mg (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: When answering a Acute vs. Chronic Priority item on the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN), which strategy maximizes your score?
options: Avoid reading lab trends and rely only on memorized general textbook definitions.
Seeing a routine dressing change or stable discharge teaching client first.
Select as many options as possible blindly regardless of +/- partial credit deductions.
Always choose 'Notify the healthcare provider' before performing a bedside assessment.
questions.rationale: Acute vs. Chronic Priority: See unstable, new-onset, post-op day 0, or bleeding clients before stable/chronic clients. Scoring rule: Seeing a routine dressing change or stable discharge teaching client first.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 6-month-old infant with Down syndrome. Which of the following interventions should be included in the nursing care plan?

Encourage regular, age-appropriate developmental stimulation
Restrict social interaction to prevent overstimulation
Avoid discussing the diagnosis with the family
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Encourage regular, age-appropriate developmental stimulation (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

Increase calcium levels
Regulate bone metabolism
Reduce kidney stone formation
questions.rationale: Calcitonin helps lower calcium levels by inhibiting osteoclast activity.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Which of the following is the most common sign of hypoxemia in this patient?
options: Tachycardia
Tachypnea
Confusion
Cyanosis
questions.rationale: In patients with COPD, the most common sign of hypoxemia is not cyanosis, tachycardia, or tachypnea, but rather acute confusion or subtle personality changes due to decreased oxygen supply to the brain.

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

options: Administer insulin
Check blood glucose levels
Encourage fluid intake
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Insulin administration helps reduce ketone production and lower blood glucose levels.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with a suspected diagnosis of Meniere's disease. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to find?
options: Tinnitus
Dry eyes
Double vision
Loss of taste
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Tinnitus (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

It is usually reversible with treatment.
It is most often caused by loud noise exposure.
It can be corrected with a cochlear implant.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: It is most often caused by loud noise exposure. (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?

"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Diabetes Mellitus, DKA vs. HHS & Insulin Peak/Onset Profiles. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been admitted to the hospital. Which of the following findings would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
options: Decreased respiratory rate
Prolonged expiratory phase
Increased lung sounds
Absence of wheezing
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often have difficulty exhaling, leading to a prolonged expiratory phase. The other options are not typical findings in COPD.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with SIADH vs. Diabetes Insipidus (Hypothyroidism, Hyperthyroidism (Thyroid Storm) & Parathyroid). What is the priority nursing action?
options: SIADH (High ADH): Fluid overload, hyponatremia, high urine SG. DI (Low ADH): Polyuria, hypernatremia, low urine SG (<1.005).
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
questions.rationale: For SIADH vs. Diabetes Insipidus, the priority intervention is: SIADH (High ADH): Fluid overload, hyponatremia, high urine SG. DI (Low ADH): Polyuria, hypernatremia, low urine SG (<1.005). Key exam watchpoint: SIADH: Fluid restriction + 3% NS if seizures. DI: Desmopressin (DDAVP) + IV fluids.

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM) is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Lithium (Depression, Bipolar Mania, Schizophrenia, Eating & Substance Disorders). What is the priority nursing action?

Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Therapeutic 0.6–1.2 mEq/L (>1.5 toxic); low Na+ or dehydration increases toxicity!
questions.rationale: For Lithium, the priority intervention is: Therapeutic 0.6–1.2 mEq/L (>1.5 toxic); low Na+ or dehydration increases toxicity! Key exam watchpoint: Maintain normal sodium & hydration; report coarse tremor, ataxia, severe diarrhea, confusion.

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a client how to self-administer eardrops. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
options: "Lie on your side with the affected ear facing up for at least 5 minutes after administering the drops."
"You can immediately return to normal activities after administering the drops."
"Store the eardrops in the refrigerator for best results."
"You should feel immediate relief after administering the drops."
questions.rationale: Lying on the side with the affected ear facing up for at least 5 minutes allows the medication to penetrate deeply into the ear canal. Option B is incorrect because it's important to remain still for a few minutes after administering the drops to ensure they are fully absorbed. Option C is incorrect because not all eardrops need to be refrigerated. Always follow the storage instructions on the medication label. Option D is incorrect because while some medications may provide immediate relief, others may take longer to work. Always follow the instructions provided by the healthcare provider.

questions.prompt: A paediatric nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who has been prescribed amoxicillin for a bacterial infection. What is the most important instruction to give the child's parents?
options: Give the medication on an empty stomach.
Stop the medication when the child feels better.
Complete the full course of the medication.
Double the dose if the child misses a dose.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Complete the full course of the medication. (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Phenytoin (Dilantin) (GCS, Cranial Nerves, Increased ICP (Cushing's Triad) & Stroke (tPA)). What is the priority nursing action?

Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Phenytoin (Dilantin), the priority intervention is: Therapeutic range 10–20 mcg/mL; causes gingival hyperplasia. Key exam watchpoint: Push IV slowly (<= 50 mg/min) in 0.9% NS only; regular soft brushing + dental visits.

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease catecholamine production
Increase catecholamine production
Regulate blood pressure
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Reducing catecholamine levels controls blood pressure.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Client Prioritization & Mass Casualty Disaster Triage develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?

Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.

Decreased pulse rate

Check blood glucose levels

Provide oxygen therapy

"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."

questions.rationale: Correct answer: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

Respiratory rate
Blood pressure

options: Administer hydrocortisone

Encourage fluid intake
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Hydrocortisone replaces deficient cortisol, helping to manage hypotension and dehydration.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Tension Pneumothorax (Respiratory A&P, Breath Sounds, ABGs, Thoracentesis & Chest Tubes). What is the priority nursing action?

Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Tracheal deviation to unaffected side, absent breath sounds, JVD, shock.

Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.

questions.prompt: When answering a Matrix / Grid item on the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN), which strategy maximizes your score?

Avoid reading lab trends and rely only on memorized general textbook definitions.

questions.rationale: For Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000), the priority intervention is: Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency! Key exam watchpoint: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been diagnosed with lead poisoning. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?

Weight gain and increased appetite
Increased urine output
Developmental delays and irritability
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Developmental delays and irritability (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who had a laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) procedure. Which of the following is a priority nursing responsibility in the immediate postoperative period?

Protecting the patient’s eyes from injury
Administering antibiotic eye drops

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k) (Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION)). What is the priority nursing action?

Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k), the priority intervention is: Petechiae, ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematuria. Key exam watchpoint: Soft toothbrush, electric razor, avoid IM injections/NSAIDs/straining.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child weighs 18 kg and is prescribed a medication at a dosage of 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. The medication comes in a concentration of 40 mg/2 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?

2 mL
4.5 mL
9 mL

Ignore the patient's frustration about the condition

Clean the patient's ear canal
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Report the symptom to the healthcare provider (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

A normal diet
A clear liquid diet
A high-fat diet
questions.rationale: During the acute phase of gastroenteritis, a clear liquid diet is often recommended to prevent dehydration and rest the gastrointestinal tract. questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with age-related macular degeneration. Which of the following symptoms is most likely to be reported?
options: Difficulty with night vision
Loss of peripheral vision
Seeing a dark spot in the center of vision
Seeing halos around lights
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Seeing a dark spot in the center of vision (Aligned with Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?

Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
